title: Phone calls
description: Answering, calling a business, reservations, wrong numbers and messages.

items.note: 여보세요 is for the phone; in person, greet with 안녕하세요.

bad.english: I get off at the next station.
Please take a seat over here.

items.english: Excuse me, but who is this?
distractors: Excuse me, but where are you?
Sorry, who are you looking for?
Excuse me, but what's your number?

items.english: Hello, I'm on the line now.
items.note: Said when you take a call someone passed to you: literally "I have taken over the phone."

good.english: Oh, hello. I'm calling about a reservation.

items.english: One moment, I'll put them on.
distractors: One moment, I'll exchange it for you.
One moment, I'll call you back.
Hold on, I'll pass on your message.

items.note: 사장님 is how you refer to or address any shop or restaurant owner.

bad.english: Excuse me, some water over here, please.

items.english: They're not at their desk right now.
items.note: -는데요 softens the line and leaves room for the caller to go on.
distractors: They're not sitting in their seat.
They're on another call right now.
They just left for the day.

good.english: Then please pass on a message.

items.english: Would you like to leave a message?
distractors: Would you like to send a text?
Shall I read you the message?

good.korean: 네, 다시 전화해 달라고 전해 주세요.
good.english: Yes, please ask them to call me back.
No, that's fine. I'll call back.

bad.english: The food is a bit salty.

distractors: Please tell them to call me.
Please put them on the phone.

good.english: Sure, may I have your name?

bad.english: Get off at the next stop.

items.note: Phone numbers are read digit by digit in Sino-Korean numbers, with 공 for zero.

items.english: Can you give me your phone number?
distractors: Can you tell me your address?
Did you change your phone number?
Can I give you my number?

good.english: Sure, I'll text it to you.

bad.english: Thank you, I'll enjoy the meal.

items.english: Sorry, I dialed the wrong number.
distractors: Sorry, you have the wrong number.

items.note: On the phone, 거기 ("there") means the place of the person you are calling.

bad.english: Yes, thank you for the meal.

items.english: Can you hear me clearly? (staff to a customer)
items.note: 고객님 ("dear customer") is how staff address you on the phone.

good.english: No, it's cutting out a bit.

bad.english: Yes, I can see it well.

distractors: Please say that one more time.
Please speak a bit more quietly.

items.english: I'm underground, so I barely get a signal.
items.note: 터지다 ("to burst") is the everyday word for having phone reception.
distractors: It's underground here, so it's very quiet.
I'm in the basement, so I can't come out.

good.english: Then call again once you're out.

bad.english: Yes, it's the first basement floor.

distractors: You keep hanging up on me.

items.english: Is now a good time to talk?
distractors: Can I use your phone now?

good.english: Sorry, I'll call you back in a bit.

distractors: Are you on the phone now?

good.english: No, I'm in class right now.

items.english: I'm in a meeting now, so I'll call you later.
distractors: The meeting is over, so I'll call you now.
I'm in a meeting now, so please text me.
I have a meeting later, so call me now.

items.korean: 나 지금 운전 중이야. 이따가 전화할게.
items.english: I'm driving right now. I'll call you later.
distractors: I'm on the bus now. Call me later.
I'm driving now. I'll be there soon.
I just stopped driving. I'll call you now.

bad.english: Yeah, I got on the bus too.

items.english: Why didn't you answer my call?
distractors: Why did you hang up on me?
Why didn't you reply to my text?

good.english: Sorry, I was in a meeting.
Sorry, my phone was on silent.

bad.english: Yeah, I'll give it to you tomorrow.

items.english: Thank you for calling customer service.
items.note: Korean businesses often answer the phone with 감사합니다 followed by their name.
distractors: Thank you, I'll call customer service.
Thank you, where is the service center?

good.korean: 안녕하세요, 주문한 게 아직 안 왔어요.
good.english: Hi, my order hasn't arrived yet.

bad.english: Yes, nice to meet you too.

good.english: I'd like to change my address.
I'd like to check my reservation.

items.english: I'll put you through to the person in charge.
distractors: I'll give you the manager's number.
I'll ask the person in charge to call you.
The person in charge is out today.

items.english: What time are you open until?
distractors: How long does it take to get there?

good.english: We're open until ten at night.

items.english: I'm calling to make a reservation.
items.note: 전화드리다 is the humble way to say you are calling someone.
distractors: I'm calling to cancel my reservation.
I called to check my reservation.
I made a reservation by phone.

items.english: What time shall I book it for?
distractors: How many people shall I book for?
What time did you book for?
Which day would you like to book?

items.korean: 토요일 저녁 일곱 시에 두 명이요.
items.english: Two people, Saturday at seven p.m.
distractors: Two people, Sunday at seven p.m.
Seven people, Saturday at two p.m.
Two people, Saturday at seven a.m.

items.english: What name is the reservation under?
distractors: How many people is the reservation for?
When did you make the reservation?

good.english: It should be under Kim Minji.

items.english: I'd like to change my reservation time.
distractors: I'd like to book for a later time.
I'd like to cancel my reservation.
I'd like to check my reservation time.

good.english: Sure, what time would you like instead?

items.english: I'd like to cancel my reservation.
distractors: I'd like to change my reservation.
I'd like to confirm my reservation.
I'd like to make a reservation.

good.english: Sure, what name is it under?

bad.english: Yes, we have a table for two.
Sure, I'll pack it to go.

items.english: All right, your booking is cancelled.
distractors: All right, I've changed your booking.
All right, I've made the booking.

items.english: I'll check and get back to you.
distractors: Please check and get back to me.
I checked and called you back.
I'll check and send you a text.

items.english: This is the delivery driver. Are you home?
distractors: This is the taxi driver. Where are you?
Your parcel arrived. Did you get it?
This is the delivery driver. Is this your house?

items.english: I'll leave it at your door.
distractors: I'll wait in front of the door.
Please leave it at the door.
I'll bring it inside for you.

items.english: Please leave it at the security office.
items.note: Korean apartment blocks have a guard office, the 경비실, that keeps parcels.
distractors: Please pick it up from the security office.
Please leave it at my door.

bad.english: Sure, I'll give you the receipt.

distractors: Did you see my missed call?

good.english: Oh, I haven't seen it yet.
Yeah, I saw it. Sounds good!

bad.english: Yeah, I got on the bus.

items.english: Send me a message on KakaoTalk.
items.note: 카톡 (KakaoTalk) is the messenger almost everyone in Korea uses.
distractors: I'll send you a KakaoTalk message.
Did you get my KakaoTalk message?

bad.english: No, I didn't do my homework.
I don't know, I just came.

distractors: I'll tell you the address on the phone.
I sent the address by email.

items.note: A common way to end a call; literally "go on in", like wishing someone a safe way home.

items.english: Well, I'll let you go then.
distractors: Then I'll cut it for you.
